elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "The Company may assign this Agreement without HDI's consent to an affiliate..."

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "...or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets" — all three triggers present, without consent.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "HDI may not assign this Agreement without the Company's prior written consent". Retained binding-effect sentence merely binds successors and assigns and does not authorise assignment, so no contradiction.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "...which shall not be unreasonably withheld", attached directly to the Vendor consent requirement.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "and in no event to a competitor of the Company" — an absolute bar, not curable by consent as drafted.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "no change of control of the Company shall give HDI any right to terminate this Agreement"; no competing change-of-control or termination trigger appears elsewhere in the cited text.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause is asymmetric: Vendor assignment (including to a successor) requires the Company's prior written consent, so Vendor has no free successor-assignment right.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: No notice obligation appears; the Company may assign to a successor without consent and without any stated notice requirement.

No general consent regime for non-successor assignments is created; the only consent requirement runs one way (HDI assignments), and Customer non-successor/non-affiliate assignments are left unaddressed.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The reasonableness standard is stated only for the Company's consent to HDI assignments; there is no 'other assignments' consent regime to which the standard attaches.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the single inserted paragraph delivers all six preferred elements in operative language (affiliate and M&A successor carve-outs without consent, Vendor consent requirement with a not-unreasonably-withheld standard, absolute competitor bar, and express negation of any change-of-control termination right).

Fallback level is not complete (asymmetric successor right, no written-notice mechanic, no general 'other assignments' consent regime), but that is immaterial because the preferred checklist is fully met.

Minimality holds: the existing binding-effect sentence in 10.3 is retained verbatim, no words outside the checklist are deleted, and the insertion adds no extras (no survival tail, notice periods, deemed-assignment language, or remedies) beyond what the six elements require.

Intent preserved: the edit creates no new Vendor assignment exception, leaves no undefined term or dangling cross-reference, and does not disturb Section 4 termination or other commercial mechanics; the retained 'successors and assigns' binding-effect language is consistent with the new consent requirement because it allocates benefit and burden rather than granting assignment rights.

Note for the drafter (rationale only, no repair needed): the finding correctly treats the absence of any change-of-control provision as a confirmatory addition rather than a deletion; if the reviewing team wants to avoid appearing to concede a Vendor right existed, the change-of-control sentence could be framed as 'for the avoidance of doubt', though as rendered it is already sufficient.
